3R replication script (analysis.R)

How to replicate: save the block below as analysis.R, place cleaned.csv (in the export bundle) beside it, then run Rscript analysis.R. The script prints every table shown in the app; the app's numbers were verified byte-for-byte against native R output. Package citations are in section 6.
# Reproducible analysis script generated by Telos
# Run from the folder holding cleaned.csv. Uncomment install.packages() the first time.
# install.packages(c("coin", "effectsize", "ggplot2"))
library(coin)
library(effectsize)
library(ggplot2)
d <- read.csv("cleaned.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
d[["gender"]] <- factor(d[["gender"]])

# === 01 · Mann-Whitney U ===
df <- data.frame(score = d[["absences"]], g = factor(d[["gender"]]))
res <- wilcox.test(d[["absences"]] ~ factor(d[["gender"]]), correct = TRUE, alternative = "two.sided")
print(res)
print(coin::wilcox_test(score ~ g, data = df))
print(effectsize::rank_biserial(score ~ g, data = df))
print(ggplot(data.frame(group = factor(d[["gender"]]), score = d[["absences"]]), aes(group, score)) +
  geom_boxplot(fill = "#9cc2ec", colour = "#0c447c") + labs(x = NULL, y = NULL))

\begin{tabular}{llllll}

\includegraphics{figures/01_mann-whitney-u/figure_boxplot.png}

The nonparametric counterpart to the independent t-test, comparing whole distributions via ranks rather than means. A p below alpha means one group's values tend to be systematically higher or lower (stochastic dominance) - this equals a difference in medians only when the two groups have similar distribution shapes. r gives the effect size. Your significance threshold ($\alpha$) is 0.05. Method: Wilcoxon rank sum test with continuity correction.

A Mann-Whitney U test gave U=7656, Z=0.85, p = .394, r=.06 [$-$.08, .21].

Statistical basis: Mann-Whitney U test (Mann, H. B., Whitney, D. R. (1947). "On a test of whether one of two random variables is stochastically larger than the other." Annals of Mathematical Statistics, 18(1), 50-60.); Rank-biserial effect size r (Ben-Shachar MS, Lüdecke D, Makowski D (2020). "effectsize: Estimation of Effect Size Indices and Standardized Parameters." Journal of Open Source Software, 5(56), 2815.).

**Question:** nonparametric two-group comparison

**Scenario:** Campus study: do absence counts (skewed) differ by gender?

## Input configuration

- **Dataset:** `campus-study.csv`
- **Configure-data:** app defaults (auto-detected types/levels)
- **Options:** continuity correction ON; two-tailed; α 0.05

| `gender` | group |
